components.reason: Implements USB_C_INPUT per PWR-001, replacing the USB_B_Micro symbol currently on J1. 16-pin USB 2.0-only Type-C receptacle: exposes VBUS, GND, CC1, CC2, D+/D- (both A6/B6 and A7/B7 pairs shorted at the symbol) and no SS pairs, which is exactly the pin set the architecture needs and keeps routing feasible on a 2-layer stackup (COST-001, MECH-003). Through-hole/SMT hybrid edge-mount part with board-edge alignment pegs, standard commodity availability. NOTE: this is a symbol/footprint substitution on J1 - it must be confirmed that J1 is not a protected object before the schematic designer applies it (TEST-004).
verified_constraints: PWR-001: USB-C receptacle supplying 5 V VBUS
PWR-003: VBUS contact current rating exceeds the 500 mA USB default budget
IF-004: provides D+/D- pair to U1.USB_D+/USB_D-
COST-001: commodity edge-mount receptacle, no BGA
MECH-003: USB 2.0-only variant, no SS pairs, routable in 2 layers

components.reason: USB_CC_PULLDOWNS block: 5.1 kOhm from each of CC1 and CC2 to GND is the USB Type-C specified Rd termination that advertises a default-power sink to the source, which is what makes a Type-C host supply 5 V on VBUS at all. Two separate resistors (not one shared) so cable orientation is detected in either flip. 1% thin-film 0603 keeps the value inside the Rd window over tolerance.
verified_constraints: PWR-001: enables 5 V VBUS delivery from a Type-C source (Rd = 5.1 k)
PWR-003: advertises USB default power sink, consistent with the 500 mA budget
COST-001: commodity 0603 chip resistor

components.reason: LDO_3V3 block: fixed 3.3 V LDO fed from 5 V VBUS. Chosen for 1 A output capability (block asks for 800 mA available against 520 mA required) and for the SOT-223 tab package, which the architecture explicitly identified as the acceptable thermal option with copper pour - at 5 V in / 3.3 V out and 500 mA the dissipation is (5.0-3.3) x 0.5 = 0.85 W, so the tab must be tied to a GND copper area on both layers. Output tolerance is well inside the +/-5% of PWR-002, and only 2 external 10 uF capacitors are required, keeping BOM cost low. If tighter thermal margin is wanted, a 5 V-to-3.3 V synchronous buck is the alternative, but that adds an inductor and violates the COST-001 preference for commodity linear regulation.
verified_constraints: PWR-002: fixed 3.3 V output, tolerance within +/-5%
PWR-002: 5 V input is within the input voltage range and above dropout
PWR-003: 1 A rating covers the 500 mA budget with margin
PWR-004: requires 10 uF input and 10 uF output capacitors, provided by C1/C2
COST-001: commodity SOT-223 LDO, no BGA

components.reason: 10 uF X5R 0805 serving three roles: VBUS_INPUT_FILTER bulk, LDO_3V3 output capacitor (required for regulator stability), and the RAIL_3V3_DECOUPLING bulk capacitor mandated by PWR-004. 16 V rating gives 3.2x derating on the 5 V VBUS node and ~5x on +3V3, so the DC-bias capacitance loss of the X5R dielectric stays modest. 0805 is chosen over 0603 for exactly that DC-bias/effective-capacitance reason at 10 uF.
components.reference_group: C1 (VBUS bulk), C2 (LDO output), C3 (+3V3 bulk)
verified_constraints: PWR-004: provides the >=10 uF bulk capacitor on the +3V3 rail
PWR-002: satisfies the LDO output capacitor requirement
16 V rating >= 3x the 5 V VBUS working voltage
COST-001: commodity MLCC

components.reason: 100 nF X7R 0603 local decoupling required by PWR-004 at every IC power pin (U1.3V3 and U2.VCC, each to be placed within 5 mm of the pin), plus one high-frequency bypass on the VBUS input filter alongside the 10 uF bulk. The fourth part is the optional EN_PULLUP RC capacitor from U1.EN to GND, which together with the 10 kOhm pull-up gives a ~1 ms power-on delay so EN releases after the +3V3 rail is valid; it is listed as optional pending the architecture's open question on EN RC scope. X7R chosen over X5R for the wider stable temperature range, matching the TEMP-001 ambient span.
components.reference_group: C4 (U1.3V3), C5 (U2.VCC), C6 (VBUS HF), C7 (EN RC, optional)
verified_constraints: PWR-004: 100 nF ceramic per IC power pin (U1, U2)
TEMP-001: X7R stable over -55 to +125 degC, covering -25 to +85 degC
50 V rating >= 10x the 5 V/3.3 V working voltages
COST-001: commodity MLCC

components.reason: EN_PULLUP block: 10 kOhm from U1.EN to +3V3 per PWR-005, so the module is enabled at power-on instead of EN being hard-tied to the rail (which is the present netlist state - U1.8 sits directly on +3V3). 10 kOhm draws only 330 uA from the rail and pairs with optional C7 for a power-on delay. 1% part for a defined RC time constant.
verified_constraints: PWR-005: 10 kOhm nominal pull-up from U1.EN to +3V3
Static current 3.3 V / 10 k = 0.33 mA, within the block's 0.4 mA budget
COST-001: commodity 0603 chip resistor

components.reason: I2C_PULLUPS block: 4.7 kOhm from each of SDA and SCL to +3V3 per IF-002. With a two-node bus (U1 master, U2 slave) the bus capacitance is well under the 400 pF I2C limit, so 4.7 k gives a rise time of roughly 0.85 x R x C = ~1 us at 100 pF - comfortably inside the 1000 ns standard-mode budget of IF-001. Sink current at V_OL is under 0.7 mA per line, inside both devices' open-drain ratings.
verified_constraints: IF-002: 4.7 kOhm pull-up on SDA and on SCL to +3V3
IF-001: rise time supports >=100 kHz standard mode at the expected bus capacitance
Combined pull-up current ~1.4 mA, within the block's 1.5 mA budget
COST-001: commodity 0603 chip resistor

components.reason: ADDR_SELECT block: 0 Ohm jumper tying U2.ADD0 to GND to fix the TMP102 address at 0x48 per IF-003. The net list already places U2.5 on GND, so this part is a placement/option component rather than a functional addition - it lets the address be changed to 0x49 later by moving the jumper to +3V3 without a board respin. If the schematic designer prefers a hard copper tie, this line can be dropped from the BOM with no requirement impact.
verified_constraints: IF-003: ADD0 tied low, selecting TMP102 address 0x48
COST-001: commodity 0603 jumper resistor

components.reason: MCU_ESP32 block: concrete part behind the existing abstract U1 symbol. The -32E-N4 is the current production variant (4 MB flash, ESP32-D0WD-V3 die) of the module already declared, so no netlist change is needed for pins 3V3/GND/GPIO21/GPIO22/GPIO25/EN. Runs directly from the +3V3 LDO rail and drives the I2C bus at 3.3 V logic. Two caveats for the schematic designer: (a) the module has an antenna keep-out that must overhang the board edge, which the 110 x 65 mm outline easily accommodates; (b) ESP32-D0WD has NO native USB peripheral, so the USB_D+/USB_D- pins on the abstract symbol do not correspond to real module pins - see U4 below.

components.reason: TEMP_SENSOR_TMP102 block: concrete part behind the existing U2 symbol. Digital I2C temperature sensor with accuracy far better than the +/-2 degC of TEMP-001 across the whole -25 to +85 degC window, 3.3 V-compatible supply, and ADD0 pin for the 0x48 address strap required by IF-003. 10 uA quiescent current makes its contribution to the VBUS budget negligible (block budget 0.02 mA). SOT-563 is the standard commodity package; it should be placed away from the LDO and the ESP32 module so self-heating from those parts does not bias the ambient reading.

components.reason: VBUS_INPUT_FILTER / USB_DATA_LINK ESD element. The connector is the only user-touchable interface on the board, and the block explicitly calls for 'bulk_and_esd'. USBLC6-2SC6 is the standard choice: two low-capacitance rail-to-rail TVS channels for D+/D- plus a VBUS clamp in one SOT-23-6, with only 1.5 pF line capacitance so it does not disturb the 90 Ohm full-speed pair of IF-004. Placed immediately at J1, before the pair fans out. Flagged for the systems owner: this is a NEW component, so it needs approval under the propose-changes-only mandate and confirmation that it does not touch a protected object.
verified_constraints: IF-004: 1.5 pF typical line capacitance preserves USB 2.0 full-speed signal integrity
PWR-001/PWR-003: VBUS clamp rated above the 5 V rail, no series current limit added
COST-001: commodity SOT-23-6, no BGA

components.reason: The netlist wires J1.D+/D- straight to U1.USB_D+/USB_D-, but ESP32-WROOM-32 (ESP32-D0WD die) has no USB peripheral - those pins do not exist on the real module, so as drawn the USB_D+/USB_D- nets cannot be built and will not satisfy IF-004. A USB-UART bridge is the standard resolution: CP2102N sits between the connector's D+/D- and the module's UART0 (TXD0/RXD0), and its RTS/DTR lines can drive the EN and IO0 straps for auto-programming. It needs only a 100 nF + 4.7 uF supply decoupling network and runs from VBUS or +3V3 with an internal regulator, so it is cheap and 2-layer friendly. This part is CONDITIONAL: it requires the systems owner to approve a new block plus a change to the U1 symbol's exposed pins (UART instead of USB), which is outside the current abstract symbol. The alternative resolution - leaving D+/D- as abstract symbol pins - must then be recorded as an explicit ERC waiver against TEST-001/IF-004.
components.reference_group: U4 (conditional - resolves the 'ESP32 native USB' open question)
